messages.subject: Accessing the Open Tree of Life with R
messages.subject_clean: Accessing the Open Tree of Life with R
messages.body_plain:
<http://www.gbif.org/newsroom/uses/2016-michonneau-et-al>

Phylogenetic trees can be tricky to assemble, but advances in genetic
sequencing and informatics has made the process significantly easier.
Still, published phylogenies are often only available as image files with
no standard for storage and representation. The Open Tree of Life (OTL)
project aims to change this, allowing researchers to assemble and maintain
phylogenies in standardized environment. Using a new software package,
rotl, researchers can now use the popular data processing suite, R, to
directly interact programmatically with the OTL data. The present paper
describes how researchers can extract relationships between taxa, but also
access phylogenies from specific studies of interest. Species data accessed
via rotl can easily be integrated with GBIF-mediated occurrences to
visualize occurrences associated with a specific study. The rotl package
fits well into the range of R tools available to biodiversity researchers.

Lep dan, Tomi
